_doc: Per-language rules of graph.extract.ts_generic (code: graph.extract.ts_lang), keyed by the langs.json lang name. vis_name / vis_cap: [regex, vis] lists tried on the def name / on the @vis capture text (first hit wins), vis_default otherwise. roots: top-level functions by name (pkg = regex on the package name the file declares). blank_names: names that bind nothing (`var _ I = (*T)(nil)`, `const _: () = ...`): a def of such a name is not a definition and a use of it is not a use. attrs: [regex on the path of the @attr text (and of the attributes wrapped in it, attr_wrap: wrapper -> number of leading arguments that are no attribute, so `unsafe(no_mangle)` and `cfg_attr(feature = "py", pyclass)` root like the plain attribute), kind] roots of the def that follows the attribute. comment_roots: group 1 of the regex is the name of a top-level def (//export, //go:linkname: a symbol another object file or the runtime links to). comment_exec: group 1 are the command words of a directive comment, the ones that look like paths become exec refs. strip_groups: [prefix, closing character] pairs, each balanced group that starts with the prefix is removed from a ref name before name_sub (the last character of the prefix opens the group: rust `::<` drops the turbofish `::<Vec<u8>>` of `Wrapper::<Vec<u8>>::new`, which no regex can balance). name_sub: [regex, replacement] applied to ref names in order (rust: a string literal inside an attribute, the quoted function name of a serde default or deserialize_with, is a weak use of that name; a qualified path `<T as Trait>::f` or `<T>::f` names no path, it is a member f of some type: `_.f`). dyn_prefix: prepended to the text of a @dyn site. recv_sub: [regex, replacement] applied in order to the type of an impl header (the qual of its methods is Type.method; a type with no name becomes _). import: parser of the @import capture (rust-use: use / mod declarations -> Import facts, go-alias: import specs -> package aliases whose x.F calls are written as the bare F; the package name is read from the last path element, `lib/v2` -> lib and v2 (a module major version or a directory `package v2`), `go-foo` -> foo: a package whose name differs from its directory is not known to a one-file extractor; bare_unknown_recv (go): a plain receiver that is no alias and no local of the definition may be such a package (`import '.../internal/store'`, `package storage`, `storage.New()`), so its x.F is recorded as the bare F as well; a local, parameter or range variable of the same name as an alias shadows the package inside its function, the extractor then records both F and x.F, queries @local). mod_path: regex (group 1 = the file) of a path attribute among the attributes that sit right before a `mod x;` declaration, also inside cfg_attr: `#[path = "sys/unix.rs"] mod imp;` imports that file relative to the directory of the declaring file and binds it as imp (the plain `mod imp;` imports imp.rs / imp/mod.rs); every path found is an import (`#[cfg_attr(unix, path = "a.rs")] #[cfg_attr(not(unix), path = "b.rs")]`); a path attribute inside an inline module is read from the directory of the file, the names of the inline modules are not added. item_macros: regex of the macros whose body holds items (`cfg_if::cfg_if! { if #[cfg(unix)] { mod unix; use unix as plat; } else { .. } }`): the body is raw tokens to the grammar, so its `mod x;` and `use ..;` declarations (with the attributes before them) are read from the text of the body and are imports like those outside a macro; the fn, struct and other items in such a body are no definitions (an item that is missing is never reported dead). protocol_names: methods of a type with these names satisfy an interface of the stdlib or a library, grouped in the list by interface (container/heap, net/http, io, sql, encoding, fmt, flag and pflag Value, sync.Locker, go/ast.Visitor, hash.Hash, log/slog.Handler, net.Listener and net.Conn, context.Context, io/fs, crypto.Signer, logrus, prometheus, zap, gorm, k8s and controller-runtime); they are called through the interface and never by name in the project (flag protocol; the linker already knows String, Error, Len, Less, Swap, Read, Write, Close ... for every language). A method is protocol by its name alone: a type that implements an interface the list does not know keeps its methods only through a caller by name. Every rule may carry strength (default hard) and trust (default convention). A def-level root also roots the file of the def (link.py), so an in-file #[test] must not be kind test: the test group seeds every node of the rooted file and would turn all dead code of a file with a tests module into test-only; it is the soft annotation root annotation:rust-test (alive only weakly) instead. Every ts_generic lang needs an entry; {} = none here (c, cpp, csharp keep their rules in queries/<grammar>/rules.json).
